Commentary.Commentary: So 158 is what Ireland need to level the series and get 10 points in the World Cup Super League. They could not get 192 in the last game will they be able to chase this below par total? Netherlands will back themselves as the pitch is not an easy one to bat on. Join us for the chase to find out.

It was once again the pace of Josh Little that wreaked havoc in the hosts batting. He bettered his 3-fer from the last game and turned it in to a 4-wicket haul . Young too was impressive and just like last game repeated what Little did and finished with a 4-fer himself. Finishing with the best figures of the innings with 4/18. McCarthy and Balbirnie kept things tight and scalped one wicket apiece. Simi Singh was the only bowler who finished wicketless. The Irish though will be little disappointed not to bowl Netherlands out and under 150. But overall a fantastic bowling display from Ireland.

Opting to bat, Netherlands got off to a solid start as Max O'Dowd gave them a steady start along with Steph Myburgh. But both the batters went back to the pavilion in quick succession. The hosts though never got any valuable stands and though a few batters got start none of them could capitalize on it. Wickets fell at regular junctures. It could have been a lot worse but thanks to valuable contributions from Logan van Beek and Brandon Glover, the hosts ended up with some respectability and a score of over 150

An excellent bowling display from Ireland and they have improved further from their bowling display from the last game. Unlike the previous game, there was no telling heroics from the lower middle order for Netherland as they have stuttered their way to 157.
OUT! TAKEN! That is a simple catch! Length and on off, Saqib chips it to covers and it is taken in the end. NETHERLANDS END WITH 157!
Commentary.Howout: c William Porterfield b Craig Young

Commentary.Commentary: Another wide! Outside off, a slower one does not come out right. Saqib swings but misses.
Fuller and on off, it is hit hard to mid off.
Wide! Down the leg side. It is wided.
TOP EDGE AND FOUR! Handy runs! Logan comes down the track and this is bowled short on the body. He pulls, it goes off the top edge down to the fine leg fence.
In the air.. safe! Angled into the batter. Logan swings, he gets a top edge. It goes up in the air towards deep mid-wicket. The fielder runs in and dives but does not get to it. No run taken again.
Fuller and on middle, it is worked through mid-wicket for one.
EDGY FOUR! 150 is up! Length and on off, this one straightens. Van Beek looks to defend, it goes off the outside edge down to the third man fence.
Fuller and on middle, it is hit hard down to long on. Cant run.

Zulfiqar makes room and does manage to guide it down to third man but for no runs. Logan will probably go for it in the next over.
On off, it is pushed to cover.
Shorter and on middle, Saqib looks to defend but it pops off the splice and lands short of the bowler.

Good length and on off, this is pushed to cover.

NOT OUT! No edge on it and the impact is umpire's call so they do not lose the review. Length and just outside off. This jags back in. Logan looks to flick but misses to get hit on the pads. On middle, it is kept out.

Klaassen looks to defend but misses it completelty. A huge appeal follows and the umpire raises his finger. Klaassen has a chat with van Beek and the pair decide to take it upstairs. Time for the Ballk Tracker and it brings bad news for Fred Klaassen as it shows three reds.
Outside off, Klaassen pushes it to mid off.
Full outside off, van Beek drives it to the right of point for one.
Fuller on off, van Beek keeps it out.

Appeal for LBW but turned down. Floated outside off, van Beek looks to sweep but misses. There is a huge appeal but it is turned down as the impact is outside off stump. The batters meanwhile take a rin as the ball goes behind point.

Floated on off, Logan defends it.
Tossed up on off, van Beek keeps it out.

Full outside off, tempting Klaassen to drive but he lets it go to the keeper.

OUT! EDGED AND GONE! The Player of the Match from the last game cannot make an impact like the previous game with the bat. Young gets his 3-fer just like the previous game. Good length ball outside off, van der Gugten looks to punch it off the back foot but the ball shapes away and catches the outside edge. It goes to the right of Tucker and he makes no mistake with the gloves on.

Commentary.Commentary: Hits the deck hard now on off. Van der Gugten hops and blocks.
Ohh! Beautiful bowling. Good seam position. It is fuller around off, van der Gugten looks to drive but the bal shapes away and beats him up.
A little bit of air on this one. It is blocked by van Beek.
Floated on the stumps, van Beek keeps it out.

Fires one quicker on the stumps. van Beek blocks it.
On the pads and short. Timm van der Gugten glances it towards fine leg for one.

Fuller on middle and off, van der Gugten tucks it to square leg.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! There was a noise as the ball went past the bat and Ultra Edge shows that the ball did hit the bat. Edwards' fighting counterattack comes to an end. Good length ball around off, Edwards looks to play it straight down the ground. The ball goes very close to the bat and the bat also hits the pad. There is some noise and the Ireland players think it is of the bat hitting the ball and going straight to Tucker, but the umpire does not. Balbirnie reviews it straightaway. Replay rolls in and Ultra Edge shows spike as the ball passes the bat. Edwards has to walk back.
Commentary.Howout: c Lorcan Tucker b Craig Young

Commentary.Commentary: Good length ball around off, Edwards defends it to the off side.
Length ball outside off, the ball dies on its way to the keeper. Tucker fails to hold onto it and they steal a bye.
The Dutch physio is seen calling him back and Zulfiqar is going back and rightly so. Van Beek walks out to bat and also Young is back on.
Flighted on off, Edwards pushes it to cover.
Shorter on off and middle. Zulfiqar ships it to fine leg and gets a single.
Darted fuller around off, Zulfiqar blocks it.
Tossed up around off, Zulfiqar strokes it through point but is unable to run.

Zulfiqar is getting treated and the umpires have called for Drinks! This is not good, Netherlands are in trouble! This stand seems to be going along nicely but if Zulfiqur does not continue, it's going to be a big blow for them. We will have to wait and see what happens. He is continuing.

NOT OUT! Zulfiqar has made his crease by just a fraction. He did not put his bat inside the crease in the last game and was out. This time he makes the same mistake but luckily he had his foot inside the crease.  Floated on middle, Edwards tucks it to the on side for a quick run. Seems like Zulfiqar pulls his hamstring during the stride of his run. The throw at the keeepr's end is a good one. Tucker whips the bails off quickly and puts in an appeal. Play and a miss to finish the over. But an expensive comeback for Little. 10 off the first over of his new spell. He gave away just 14 in his 5 overs of the first spell. Full outside off, Edwards looks to drive but misses,
This one keeps low! Fullish outside off, Edwards looks to defend but the ball keeps low and beats him.
Inside edge but safe! Fullish outside off, Edwards looks to drive it square on the off side but it goes off the inside edge away from the stumps and fine leg for a brace.
Full around off, Edwards drives it straight to mid off.
FOUR! Back-to-bak boundaries. Edwards' positive approach is reaping rewards. Full outside off, Edwards looks to drive but it goes off the outside edge though third man for a boundary.
FOUR! False start for Little to his new spell. He starts with a full toss around off, Edwards slams it through covers for a boundary.
On middle, it is eased down to long on for one. A really good over then for Netherlands.
Two more! On the pads, this is worked towards fine leg for two.
FOUR! Swept and done so brilliantly! On middle, this is swept through backward square leg. No chance for the man in the deep. Edwards looking positive.
On middle, this is eased down to long on for one.
Really good improvisation! Brings the reverse sweep out and plays it all along the ground through backward point for three.

On middle, it is played back to the bowler.

OUT! THREE REDS AND DE LEEDE HAS TO WALK BACK! Not sure why he reviewed there as he had started walking back even before he was given out. Both the set batters are out of here now. Ireland well and truly on top now. This is shortish and quicker. De Leede, throughout his innings was content to play back which is a risk on this wicket and he pays the price. Goes back and this one skids through and stays low. It hits his pad right in front. He almost started walking before the finger was raised. He then turned back, had a word with his partner and reviewed it. Replays show that it is as plumb as it can get.
Bas de Leede has been adjudged LBW but he has decided to take it upstairs.  Will technology come to his rescue? Big moment in this game.
Another one on middle, this is nudged to the man at mid-wicket.
On middle, this is worked to mid-wicket.
On middle, blocked.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! The change in bowling works wonders and Young gets the wicket his side needed. That is a lazy stroke from Seelaar. It is on a length and well outside off, Seelaar plays it with an open face of the bat very loosely. It goes off the outside edge and to the keeper. Ireland remain on top as they have broken through a stand which was starting to build.

Commentary.Commentary: Shorter and on off, this is guided down to third man for one.

Outside off, this is guided down to third man for another run.
Shorter and on the body, it is worked down to fine leg for one.
Change in bowling. Craig Young is back on. 0/11 from his 4 overs so far.

Gets the sweep out but finds the man at short fine leg again.
On middle, it is worked to mid-wicket.

On middle, this is worked to mid-wicket.

Outside off, this stays low. Seelaar looks to push at it but is beaten.

An appeal for caught behind follows but the umpire is unmoved. Andy Balbirnie decides to review it. Replay rolls in and Ultra Edge shows no movement when the ball goes past the bat. Bas de Leede survives.
Review time! Ireland feel they have their man caught behind but the on-field umpire does not. Let's see if the replays work in favour of Ireland.

Seelaar looks to sweep but finds the man at short fine leg.

Shorter and on middle, this is pulled through square leg for one.
On middle, this is nudged around the corner for one.

Just outside off, left alone nicely.
Fuller again and on middle, this is played back to the bowler.
Two more to the total! This is full and on the pads, it is worked down to fine leg for a couple.

Fuller and on the pads, this is worked to mid-wicket.
On middle, this is nudged on the leg side for another single.

Good length ball wide outside off. Seelaar leaves it alone.

Tossed up around off, Seelaar strokes it through covers and gets a brace to finish the over. 6 off McBrine's first.
FOUR! Smart cricket! The Dutch skipper gets off the mark with a boundary. Flighted around off, Seelaar gets down on his knee and sweeps it fine down the leg side for a boundary.

Change in bowling. Josh Little's fruitful spell comes to an end and he is replaced by Andy McBrine!

Excellnet over from the left-arm pacer. Wicket maiden! The last ball is on a length on the stumps. Seelaar blocks it.

Length ball on middle and off, Seelaar starts his innings with a back foot defense.
Good length ball around off, Seelaar keeps it out.
Skipper Pieter Seelaar walks out to bat now.

DRINKS! Netherlands were going nicely but Little has turned the game on its head and put the tourists in command of this game. He has looked superb and got another 3-fer. He will be looking to add more to this. Netherlands need a partnership here and the wicket of O'Dowd has certainly pushed them on the back foot.

OUT! BOWLED! An absolute beauty from Little. He bowls a peach of a delivery to give his side the big wicket of Max O'Dowd! The change of angle from the left-arm seamer does the job. He comes around the wicket, uses the width of the crease and bowls it around off. Max O'Dowd looks to defend but the ball comes in and goes past the outside edge to hit the top of off stump.
Length ball on middle and off, O'Dowd keeps it out.
Flighted on middle, de Leede keeps it out.
FOUR! Short and punished! It is around off, de Leede gets on his back foot and pulls it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Tossed up on off, O'Dowd nudges it to cover for one.
Around off, O'Dowd keeps it out.
Floated on the pads, de Leede comes down the track and tickles it over leg slip for a single.
Floated on the pads, Bas keeps it out.
Outside off, Max leaves it alone.
Full on middle and leg, O'Dowd shuffles inside and whips it away from fine leg for a brace.
Another one outside off, going away with the angle. O'Dowd keeps his bat inside the line of the stump.
Good length ball outside off, O'Dowd looks to defend but misses.
Another steepy ball. Back of a length ball outside off, O'Dowd keeps his bat inside the line and lets it go to the keeper.
Shortish ball on middle. O'Dowd blocks it.
Floated outside off, Bas looks to play but misses.
Edged but falls short! Floated on middle and leg, Bas de Leede looks to defend but it hits the inside edge onto the pads. The ball lobs behind but falls short of the man at leg slip.
Floated around off, de Leede keeps it out.
FOUR! Bas de Leede gets off the mark in style! Short around off, de Leede gets on his back foot and pulls it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Short around off, O'Dowd punches it to the left of Balbirnie at mid off and takes a single.
Loopy ball on off, O'Dowd pushes it back to the bowler.

Edged but does not carry! Fullish ball in the channel of uncertainty around off. Bas de Leede looks to defend but gets a feather on it. Luckily for de Leede it falls well short of Tucker.
Length ball outside off, Bas leaves it alone.
WIDE! Down the leg side. De Leede looks to flick but misses.
Bas de Leede denies Little the hat-trick. Good length ball on middle and off, it is bowled at good pace. Bas de Leede manages to block it.
Who will walk out to face the hat-trick ball? It will be Bas de Leede!

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Little gets two-in-two and he is on a hat-trick now. The pace of Little gets the better of Cooper once again. A golden duck for Cooper. Little dishes in a short ball. It is bowled at pace and it is directed superbly too. It is around off, Cooper looks to defend but the ball shapes away and catches the outside edge of Ben's willow. It goes straight into the mitts of Lorcan Tucker and he is not going to drop those.
Commentary.Howout: c Lorcan Tucker b Josh Little

Commentary.Commentary: Ben Cooper walks out at number 3!

OUT! CHOPPED ON! Little strikes and Ireland get the first breakthrough.  The pace of Little has got the better of Myburgh. Good length ball on off, it nips back in just a bit. Myburgh looks to play the cut but the ball is too close to him to play that shot. It comes on quickly as well. Myburgh looks to cut but gets an inside edge onto the stumps.  A wicket Ireland needed as this partnership was looking settled.
Tossed up on the stumps, Max blocks it to see off the over. 5 off this over. Simi's most expensive one so far in this game.
Shorter on middle and off, O'Dowd tucks it to the on side.
Quicker and turning in from outside off. O'Dowd looks to defend but misses.
Floated on off, O'Dowd keeps it out.
FOUR! Very well played! Flighted delivery around off, O'Dowd gets down on his knee and sweeps it right off the middle through backward square leg for a boundary.
Floated on middle, Myburg pushes it through mid off for one.
Fuller on middle, O'Dowd punches it to mid on.
Short ball! A very well directed one as well. It is quick and on middle and off, O'Dowd does well to sway away.
Good length ball which nips back in from middle. O'Dowd does well to block it.
FOUR! Nicely played! Little bowls it too straight on the pads, O'Dowd whips it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Length ball on off, this time O'Dowd blocks it to cover.
Good length ball around off, O'Dowd taps it to the left of backward point.
Bounce again. This is on off, Myburgh looks to defend but does so off the upper half of his bat.
Turn and bounce! This pitches on off, Myburgh looks to defend but the ball turns away with good bounce and beats the outside edge of Myburgh's willow.
WIDE! Darted quicker but down the leg side. Myburgh looks to sweep but misses. Lorcan Tucker quickly whips the bails off and puts in an appeal but the umpire is not keen. He just signals it as wide.
Shorter on off, Myburgh cannot buy a run at the minute against Simi as he blocks this too.
Flighted around off, this one keeps a bit low. Stephan Myburgh does well to defend it.
Tossed up on middle, Myburgh keeps it out.
Short around off, Myburgh punches it half-heartedly to cover.
Powerplay 2 signaled by the umpire. Now maximum of 4 players can be placed outside the 30-yard circle till the 40th circle.
A length ball, outside off, Max O'Dowd looks to block it but misses as the ball zips past the outside edge.
A length ball, on off, Max O'Dowd pushes it to cover.

A length ball, outside off, left alone.

A length ball, outside off, Myburgh pushes it to cover.

A loopy ball, on off, Myburgh pushes it to mid off.

A length ball, outside off, Max O'Dowd watches it go to the keeper.
A touch fuller, on pads, Max O'Dowd flicks it to deep mid-wicket as they come back for the second comfortably.

We are all set for the action to begin! The Ireland players make their way out on the field. Max O'Dowd and Stephan Myburgh stride out to open the innings for Netherlands. Barry McCarthy to start the proceedings with the new ball for Ireland.

Ireland skipper, Andy Balbirnie, says that they would have had a bat as well. Tells they bowled well the other day but admits things went away from them towards the end. Tells rotating the strike is crucial and admits they did not do that at the top in the last game. Tells Little has been the fittest he has ever been and gives them the extra option. Balbirnie informs they are unchanged too.

Netherlands skipper, Pieter Seelaar says the pitch has not changed and hopes they can put a better batting performance. Seelaar says that they pride themselves on their bowlers. Seelaar says that getting in was the hardest part for the batter. Seelaar says that these wickets help his bowling. Seelaar says that it is going to be a hard game and tells scoring won't be easy. Informs they are unchanged.

PITCH REPORT - Niall O'Brien and Peter Borren are the pitch analysts for the day. O'Brien says there is glorious sunshine. Borren says the batter can either take their time and settle in or go after it straightaway. O'Brien says the pitch might be similar to the last game.
Ireland Playing XI - Paul Stirling, William Porterfield, Andrew Balbirnie (C), Harry Tector, George Dockrell, Lorcan Tucker (WK), Simi Singh, Andy McBrine, Barry McCarthy, Joshua Little, Craig Young.

Netherlands Playing XI -  Max ODowd, Stephan Myburgh, Ben Cooper, Pieter Seelaar (C), Bas de Leede, Scott Edwards (WK), Logan van Beek, Saqib Zulfiqar, Brandon Glover, Timm van der Gugten, Fred Klaassen.
TOSS - Time for the coin flip. It falls in Pieter Seelaar's way. NETHERLANDS OPT TO BAT!

Hello and welcome to game number two of the three match ODI series between Netherlands and Ireland. A nail-bitter is what we witnessed in the first game where the hosts came out on top. This is a must win for the visitors if they are to stay alive in the series. Let’s hope for another cracker of a game.
